title: Implement store::write and the tolerant reader
description: Implement the graph 'Write to the store' in PLAN.md section 12.4 and the reader in section 3.4, with the state directory from section 3.1. Use std::fs::File locking (ADR 0002). The reader also supports reading from a byte offset for the TUI.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every E: line of the graph has a test.

title: Spike: prompt delivered to a working Claude Code
description:
## Goal

Use 'spike-send' while Claude Code is mid-turn (W13 in RESEARCH.review.md). Observe when the prompt is handled, and what happens to it when the user presses Esc before it is handled. ADR 0003 depends on the answer.

## Findings

Fill in when the spike is done: what was run, what was observed, and what it changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/adr/0003 'Consequences' states the observed behaviour for both cases.
- If a queued prompt can be lost, a follow-up bead exists for how send should report it.
close_reason: Working agent queues the prompt and answers it as the next turn; Esc interrupts the running turn and the queued prompt is then submitted, not lost. ADR 0003 updated. No follow-up needed.

title: Spike: pane id stability, decide ADR 0006
description:
## Goal

Find out when a public pane id changes and whether terminal_id survives. Try: closing a sibling pane, moving the pane to another tab, moving it to another workspace, restarting the Herdr server with session restore. Compare 'herdr pane list' before and after, and the HERDR_PANE_ID seen by a process already running in the pane.

## Findings

Fill in when the spike is done: what was run, what was observed, and what it changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/adr/0006 has status accepted or rejected, with the observed cases listed.
- If rejected, PLAN.md section 6.2 is rewritten to match and the beads that cite ADR 0006 are updated.
close_reason: ADR 0006 accepted with the observed cases. Terminal id survives moves but not a server restart, noted in PLAN.md 6.2. Not rejected, so no rewrite of 6.2 or other beads.

title: Spike: environment, action context and keys
description:
## Goal

Answer three questions on the installed Herdr and write each answer into PLAN.md section 11. (1) Do REVIEW_DELIVER_TO and REVIEW_DELIVER_TERM passed with --env reach the pane process (W15)? (2) Is an action with contexts = ["pane"] offered and runnable while the review pane is focused, and what does focused_pane_id hold then (W24)? (3) Do prefix+i and prefix+shift+i bind as plugin_action without a duplicate-key warning?

## Findings

Fill in when the spike is done: what was run, what was observed, and what it changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- PLAN.md section 11 states each answer with the command that showed it.
- An answer that contradicts the plan has a follow-up bead linked with discovered-from.
close_reason: All three answered in PLAN.md section 11; none contradicts the plan, so no follow-up bead. The pane-offered half of the action-context question can only be checked by hand with a bound key.
